text:
carla: Heads up — design wants an "Impersonate tenant" flow for tenant-admins in Console. Needs to be audit-friendly and not leak perms. Two options I sketched: UI-level "Switch context" vs server-issued ephemeral tokens. Thoughts?

anand: +1 on audit. Ephemeral tokens give clearer server-side control. Concern: routing and quotas — if tenant-admin impersonates, should requests count against the tenant or the admin? Need a policy.

lee: For billing/quotas we should attribute to the tenant. For change-control (who made the change) keep admin identity in audit logs. So token should carry tenant_id + actor_id; runtime routes by tenant_id for quota, but log actor_id.

sara: UX note — avoid full "switch user" because people forget to switch back. Add a persistent banner and an "end impersonation" CTA. Also show a short countdown for ephemeral sessions.

anand: Quick API sketch:
```
POST /api/v1/impersonate
Body: { "tenant_id": "t-1234", "actor_id": "u-5678", "scope": ["routes:invoke"], "duration": 900 }
Response: { "token": "ey..", "issued_for": "t-1234", "actor": "u-5678", "expires_at": "2025-11-01T12:34:56Z" }
```

deploy-bot: note — add audit event types IMPERSONATION_START and IMPERSONATION_END, and surface them to the audit export.

carla: Security constraints: require MFA for tenant admins to start impersonation and only allow it from IPs in the tenant allowlist if configured. Also show an "effective permissions" preview in the console before confirming.

sara: +1. Also display "will be billed to: <tenant>" and "routing policy: <policy-name>" in the preview so admins don't accidentally hit Dedicated capacity.

lee: Implementation plan: 1) API + token plumbing (eng-runtime) 2) Console UI preview + persistent banner (eng-platform) 3) Telemetry keys: impersonation_actor, impersonation_tenant, impersonation_duration 4) Rollout behind a tenant opt-in feature flag. Rough estimate: 2 sprints.

carla: I'll author a small MR for the API schema and attach design mocks. Assigning follow-ups: anand + lee for API/runtime, sara for UX. I'll post mocks in #design after lunch. :thumbsup:
